import pandas as pd

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """
    Reproduces legacy ETL: sort → dedup(keep LAST) → aggregate with NULL group preservation
    """
    # Source
    df = inputs["meter_reads"].copy()
    
    # Sort by meter_id ASC, read_ts ASC, read_seq ASC
    df = df.sort_values(
        by=["meter_id", "read_ts", "read_seq"],
        ascending=[True, True, True],
        na_position="last"
    )
    
    # Dedup: keep LAST row per meter_id
    # After sorting, groupby + tail(1) gives us the last row per key
    df = df.groupby("meter_id", dropna=False).tail(1)
    
    # Aggregate: group by zone (treating NULL as a real group), sum kwh, count rows
    df = df.groupby("zone", dropna=False, as_index=False).agg({
        "kwh": "sum",
        "meter_id": "count"
    })
    
    # Rename columns to match output schema
    df = df.rename(columns={"kwh": "total_kwh", "meter_id": "meter_count"})
    
    # Ensure column order
    df = df[["zone", "total_kwh", "meter_count"]]
    
    return {"zone_totals": df}
